NEAR's fee burn plus Intents buybacks equal 11.8% of what it mints. Break-even is 8.5x away.

10.9% is NEAR sent by the NEAR Intents contract to the buyback account, where it is held, not burnt. 0.92% is gas fees burnt. A fee-burn dashboard sees only the second number and puts break-even 109x away.

Mint, burn and the buyback balance are read from NEAR mainnet, 2026-04-05 to 2026-11-12 (731 epochs, heights 192642725 to 224221936). Mint and burn are exact to the yoctoNEAR. Rebuild with python3 run.py: no keys, no network.

Payback was 9.5% in the first window with buyback data (2026-06-29), peaked at 16.5% (2026-09-19) and is 11.8% now.

What closes the gap

Payback is burn plus buybacks over issuance. Three levers move it. Two of them are governance decisions.

Chain versus the indexer

The same flows over the same days, in NEAR a day. DefiLlama reports USD; each day is converted at that day's price.

Sender check: 248 of the last 249 transfers into the buyback account came from intents.near, carrying 99.5% of the NEAR (NearBlocks, with transaction hashes in data/inflows.csv).

The case against

  • Buybacks are held in a multisig account, not burnt. Supply does not fall and the NEAR can be spent.
  • Payback has fallen from its peak of 16.5% to 11.8%.
  • NEAR Intents is not growing: over a year, daily volume is 1.02x and gross fees 0.75x (DefiLlama).
  • One application supplies 92% of the payback.
  • Gas burn alone covers 0.92% of issuance, 109x from break-even.
